column1: # Natural alternatives for communicative moves, plus the connected situations
# that teach them. These remain ordinary sentence items; the mission catalog
# groups them into a response palette without storing an exercise in content.

column6: note

column1: # Leave the id off a new row: the build assigns one and writes it back.

column2: Hola, Luis. Soy Marta. Mucho gusto.
column3: Hello, Luis. I'm Marta. Nice to meet you.
Nice to meet you. How are you?
Very well, thank you. And you?
Hi, Luis! How are you today?

column2: Estoy genial. Tengo un día muy bueno.
column3: I'm doing great. I'm having a very good day.

column2: Bueno, tengo que irme. Hasta pronto.
column3: Well, I have to go. See you soon.

column1: # ── Un saludo en el trabajo (guided transfer) ────────────────────────────────

column3: Good morning, Luis. How are you?

column2: Estoy un poco cansado, pero bien. ¿Y usted?
column3: I'm a little tired, but fine. And you?

column2: Estoy bastante bien, gracias por preguntar.
column3: I'm quite well, thank you for asking.

column2: Me alegro. Buen día y hasta luego.
column3: I'm glad. Have a good day and see you later.

column2: Hola, soy Elena, la nueva vecina. ¿Cómo estás?
column3: Hi, I'm Elena, the new neighbour. How are you?

column2: Hoy estoy más o menos. ¿Y tú?
Bien, gracias. Estoy un poco cansada.
column3: Fine, thanks. I'm a little tired.

column2: Tienes que descansar. Nos vemos pronto.
column3: You need to rest. See you soon.

column1: # ── Response palette: natural answers to «¿Cómo estás?» ──────────────────────

column6: Very positive and energetic.
Casual and concise.
Positive, but less emphatic.
Neither especially good nor bad.
A common concise answer meaning things could be better.
Feminine speaker form; use cansado for a masculine speaker.
A gently softened tired answer for a masculine speaker.
An honest, gently softened negative answer.
A clear negative answer that can invite concern.

column1: # ── Response palette: ordering at a café ─────────────────────────────────────

column6: Short, polite and direct.

column2: Quiero un café con leche, por favor.
column3: I'd like a coffee with milk, please.
column6: A dependable full request with quiero.

column2: Para mí, un té con leche.
column3: For me, a tea with milk.
column6: Natural when ordering as part of a group.

column2: Voy a tomar un zumo de naranja.
column6: A common way to make your choice.
A minimal everyday order.

column3: I'd like a coffee without milk.
column6: Useful for removing an ingredient.
Adds a simple preference with pero.
Gently indicates that you may add something later.

column1: # ── Response palette: asking for a destination ───────────────────────────────

column3: Excuse me, where is the pharmacy?
column6: Polite and direct.

column3: Excuse me, where is the station?
column6: Slightly more formal with disculpe.

column3: Where is the town centre, please?
column6: The courtesy comes at the end.

column3: Excuse me, I'm looking for the museum.
column6: States the goal instead of asking a direct question.

column3: Do you know where the bank is?
column6: A softer indirect question.

column3: How do I get to the square?
column6: Asks for the route rather than only the location.
Useful when you already know it is in the area.

column2: Necesito ir al hotel. ¿Por dónde voy?
column3: I need to get to the hotel. Which way do I go?
column6: Explains the destination and asks for a route.

column1: # ── Response palette: saying what you want in a clothes shop ─────────────────

column3: I'm looking for a white shirt.
column6: A straightforward item-and-colour request.
Direct and easy to adapt.
Uses necesito when the item is a need.

column3: I'm looking for a green dress.
column6: A natural ongoing-search expression.

column3: Do you have this shirt in red?
column6: Keeps the item and changes the colour.
Asks for a different fit without repeating the item.
A polite way to decline help.

column2: Busco algo cómodo para el trabajo.
column3: I'm looking for something comfortable for work.
column6: Describes the quality and purpose instead of naming an item.

column1: # ── Response palette: confirming a hotel stay ────────────────────────────────

column6: The simplest confirmation.

column2: Sí, una habitación doble para una noche.
column3: Yes, a double room for one night.
column6: Gives room type and duration together.

column2: Tengo una habitación individual para dos noches.
column3: I have a single room for two nights.
column6: A full stay description without sí.

column2: La reserva está a nombre de López.
column3: The reservation is under the name López.
column6: Gives the name the receptionist needs.
A concise answer to a duration question.
Clarifies the number of guests.

column3: I have a room with breakfast.
column6: Clarifies an included option.

column2: No tengo reserva. ¿Hay una habitación libre?
column3: I don't have a reservation. Is there a room available?
column6: Handles the useful unscripted case of arriving without a booking.

column1: # ── Response palette: reacting to a suggestion ───────────────────────────────

column6: Simple positive acceptance.
Warm and enthusiastic acceptance.
Casual and decisive.

column2: Sí, pero un poco más tarde.
column6: Accepts while changing one detail.

column3: I'd prefer to go to the park.
column6: Offers an alternative rather than rejecting the plan.
A clear practical refusal.
Declines politely and gives a reason.
Keeps the relationship open after declining.

column3: I don't really feel like it.
column6: A softer personal refusal.

column3: What if we go to the cinema?
column6: Responds with a different suggestion.

column1: # ── Response palette: describing a real morning ──────────────────────────────

column2: Normalmente me despierto a las siete.
column3: I normally wake up at seven.
column6: A simple time anchor with a frequency word.
Begins a sequence clearly.
Adds the next action.

column3: I have coffee and fruit for breakfast.
column6: Personalises the routine with breakfast.

column2: Por la mañana leo las noticias.
column3: In the morning I read the news.
column6: Adds a habitual activity.

column2: Preparo el desayuno en la cocina.
column3: I make breakfast in the kitchen.
column6: Adds both an action and a place.

column2: A las ocho salgo de casa.
column6: Connects an action to a time.

column3: I go to work by bus.
column6: Adds destination and transport.

column3: On Sundays I get up late.
column6: Contrasts a weekend habit.

column2: Antes de salir, limpio un poco la casa.
column3: Before going out, I clean the house a little.
column6: Uses antes de to connect two events.
